bifrost: springboard/src/shell/photos/ (built-in Photos app, reads ~/Pictures); springboard/apps/notes-desktop/src/notes/picker.rs (camera-roll sheet). App API: springboard/sdk/src/photo_library.rs with the photos service
summary: BifrOSt has a built-in Photos app that browses a folder-based library (All Photos, Favorites, Recently Deleted, Screenshots, Recents), with thumbnails, a viewer, a slideshow, a basic editor and JPEG EXIF reading. Apps get a partial PhotoKit-style API: authorization, asset fetch, thumbnails, change observation and a picker call that the shell refuses for now. There is no Live Photo, no editing extension host and no project host.

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/photo_access.rs; springboard/ui/src/photo_changes.rs (change details of a library listing); springboard/sdk/src/photo_library.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/photos.rs
features.note: Authorization is modelled headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-07.rs (first answer kept, limited access, restricted library), and the change details a library observer would receive (inserted, removed, moved, changed, duplicate refusal) are tested in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-23.rs. Apps reach authorization_status and request_authorization through springboard/sdk/src/photo_library.rs, answered by the photos service, observers register through observe, but there is no access sheet, and the access sheet needs a display and the Midget check.

features.feature: Enhanced privacy and limited library access
features.apple: Delivering an Enhanced Privacy Experience in Your Photos App; PHPickerFilter scope
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 4 (w4-photokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Apps can read ~/Pictures without a prompt through the springboard library module. No per-asset grants are issued.

gaps: The app-facing photo library covers fetch, authorization, thumbnails and change observation; there is no asset creation, no collections, and isFavorite is always false.
The picker call exists (PHPickerViewController), but the shell refuses it: there is no picker sheet yet, so apps fall back to their own picker.
No Live Photo support in the library or the viewer (PHLivePhoto).
Movie pixel size is not read (reported as 0 x 0); movies are listed as video assets.
The editing and project contracts exist in the SDK (photo_editing.rs, photo_project.rs), but the Photos app hosts no third-party editor or project extension.
Change observation exists (observe pushes library_did_change every two seconds); there is no PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver object, and no per-asset permission grants.
Metadata is read from JPEG and PNG only (HEIC and RAW are not); no extended asset metadata object for apps.
